name: Chequered
tagline: Small indie web app in the personal tracking space; the exact feature list is unverified at time of drafting.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a small single-purpose tool on a one-word .app domain, which is the exact profile of an app whose core loop an agent can reproduce in an afternoon. What an agent cannot reproduce is the part the author spent months on: the empty states, the keyboard shortcuts, the thing that stops you from fat-fingering a whole week of data. So the honest answer is kinda, with the usual gaps: no mobile app, no sync between your laptop and your phone, no one fixing it at 2am but you. Note that we have not verified the feature list or pricing firsthand, so treat the confidence as low and check the site before you trust this verdict. If the product turns out to lean on a shared dataset or an integration we did not see, the verdict moves toward no.
coreLoopDIY: Stands up a local-first grid tracker in your browser: define the things you want to track, tick off days, see streaks and totals, with everything stored on your own machine.
requirements: no accounts, no API keys, no hosting if you run it locally
whatYouLose: Any mobile app or installable experience the real product ships
Sync across devices, which is the single hardest thing to bolt on afterwards
The hundred small interaction decisions that make a tracker pleasant instead of a chore
Whatever imports, exports or integrations exist that we did not inventory
Someone else owning the bugs and the backups
moatNotes: Trackers are sticky because the history lives in them. A year of data is a bigger lock-in than any feature.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a few dollars a month is cheaper than caring. Small indie tools like this sell the fact that someone already made the thousand micro decisions you would otherwise make badly at midnight, and they keep making them as the browser and your phone shift underneath. The build is easy; the maintenance and the taste are the product.
notes: Listed at low confidence: the shape of the build is clear, the shape of the product less so.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal tracker web app in an empty folder. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage, all data stays in the browser
- date-fns for date math
- Vitest for a handful of unit tests on the streak logic

Features that are in scope:
- Create, rename, archive and delete trackable items, each with a colour and an optional daily target number
- A chequerboard grid view per item: one cell per day, last 365 days, click a cell to toggle done or to enter a number if the item has a target
- Keyboard support: arrow keys move across the grid, space toggles, number keys enter a count
- Stats per item: current streak, longest streak, completion rate over the last 30 and 365 days
- A single dashboard listing all active items with a compact 8 week strip each
- Undo for the last 20 edits, because fat-fingering a cell is the main way this tool hurts you
- Export all data to JSON and import it back, validated with zod
- Light and dark theme following the system preference

Explicitly out of scope: multi-user support, cloud sync, auth, notifications, native mobile apps, any network request of any kind.

Structure: src/db.ts for the Dexie schema and migrations, src/lib/streaks.ts for pure date logic with tests, src/components for UI. Keep the pure logic free of React so the tests are boring.

Ship a README with setup steps, a note that data lives only in this browser profile, and a loud warning to use the JSON export as the backup. Add a .env.example only if you end up needing secrets, which you should not.

Run the dev server and the tests before you declare it done.
